sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Mainz keeps cars out of its old town step by step while raising what residents pay. Every regulation we could source here rests on one regional online paper, Mainz&, because the city's own site returned errors, so none of this comes from an official document we could read. On 1 July 2025 the city raised the fee for resident parking permits from 30 euros a year to a formula based on the size of the vehicle, which gives roughly 130 to 300 euros a year, with permits valid for at most one year from then and no social discount. Before the rise the city counted about 14,500 permits against roughly 8,900 public spaces, with about 7,600 permits in the Neustadt [11]. Free on-street parking for electric cars ended in September 2024 [12]. Since 1 August 2026 the Große Bleiche, near the Landtag, is closed to ordinary car traffic towards the Rhine, with only buses, taxis and bicycles allowed, which the council decided in June 2026 to protect the capacity of the new tram link in Binger Straße; the transport department expects about 80 percent less traffic there, and the paper reported confusion and detours [13]. That tram line went into service on 10 August 2026 [14]. For the inner city, the council decided on 9 April 2025 on a preferred route for a further tram through Ludwigstraße, Flachsmarkt, Große Bleiche and Rheinallee, with planning approval from late 2027 and opening between 2032 and 2034, which is a plan [15]. A survey of firms by the IHK Rheinhessen in August 2026 found that 78 percent of responding firms rate the effect of the traffic situation as mostly negative, and four in five said access had worsened further since 2024; the sample size is not given [16].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The development is mostly about tariffs and charging inside the garages. The municipal operator PMG announced on 31 March 2025 a night tariff, Park@Night, for 16.99 euros a month, or 26.99 euros with all of Saturday, to start on 1 July 2025; it is now offered as a one-year contract valid in 18 garages and requires a Park&Go registration [6][7]. At the presentation the Lord Mayor said the garages were only about 10 percent occupied at night, which was his statement and not a published count [9]. On 27 February 2026 PMG put 26 new charging points into service in Parkhaus Rathaus, at a flat 54 cent per kWh, with more announced for Parkhaus Löhrstraße [10]. PMG moved its garages to licence-plate recognition, the first six in 2024, and closed Parkhaus CityPort fully from 12 May to 1 June 2025 for the change [2].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
PMG Parken in Mainz GmbH, owned by the Mainzer Aufbaugesellschaft and the city, runs most central garages: about 10,000 spaces in 25 facilities by its company page, though its other pages say 27 or 28, so the count is approximate. The parking ticket also works as a bus and tram ticket of Mainzer Mobilität [0]. A city parking guidance system shows free and occupied garages from live data [1]. A typical central garage charges 0.80 euro for the first half hour, 1.00 euro for the second and third, then 2.10 euros an hour, with a daytime maximum of 10.00 euros and a night maximum of 5.00 euros [3]. Römisches Theater and CineStar have a daytime maximum of 15.50 euros, and Parkhaus Wallstraße, with 303 spaces outside the inner city, charges 3.00 euros per 24 hours [4]. PMG's stated capacities include CityPort 1,105, Taubertsberg 767, Rathaus 545, Kronberger Hof 460 and Römisches Theater 436 [8].

Our data are only just starting. The Mobilithek feed from the Stadtplanungsamt began delivering to us on 21 October 2026, so we have a single day of readings and no weekday or weekend averages yet. The feed's capacities are lower than PMG's for several garages, for example 247 for Römisches Theater and 215 for Kronberger Hof, and it includes Kupferberg (515) and Trajanstraße (225), which are not on PMG's list, so we could not identify their operators. The measured picture will follow in a later update.
